title: promote-latest refuses a --version strictly older than the current latest (paired with quest-cli; backports are not a promote use case)
description: Orchestrator ruling A (opum-agent, cross-session, 2026-09-28; being recorded in opum-doc -- cite that record by ref once it lands). Found by the LCLI-617 implementer: promoting --version 0.10.5 while latest reads 0.11.0 plans without complaint and writes a record with prior 0.11.0, which LCLI-617's rule (a prior newer than the release is refused) then refuses on BOTH resume and --rollback -- so the promotion is stranded. Both repos' comments assume promotion never moves latest backwards; neither planPromotion enforces it. Ruling: planPromotion refuses a --version strictly OLDER than the current latest, before any move, with a message naming both versions. Equal-to-latest is handled however the resume path already needs; the ruling is only about strictly older. Backports are NOT a promote use case: if one is ever needed it publishes under a non-latest dist-tag through a separate path, not built now -- the refusal message and the code comment say so, so nobody 'fixes' the refusal to allow backports. quest-cli files its twin; verdicts identical (same refuse/accept on every input, wording may differ), landed by swapping head SHAs as for LCLI-617/QCLI-391.

acceptanceCriteria.text: promote-latest.mjs planPromotion (dry run and --promote) refuses a --version strictly older than the current latest of any package it would move, before any registry write, with a message naming both versions and saying backports are not a promote use case (a separate non-latest dist-tag path, not built); a code comment says the same

The comparison uses LCLI-617 compareReleaseVersions (numeric, not lexical: promoting 0.9.0 over latest 0.10.0 is refused; 0.10.0 over 0.9.0 is not); equal-to-latest keeps its existing resume behaviour, proven by a test
quest-cli twin cited by id and both merge SHAs; verdicts confirmed identical by reading each rule by ref at the other head
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the scripts/ change

A fresh run (dry run and --promote) also refuses, before any registry write, a --version that is not plain X.Y.Z (e.g. 1.0.0-beta.1) -- latest only ever takes a release -- e.g. by validating plan.record with {version} before the first write; a test proves a prerelease --version makes zero registry writes. The refusal message says a prerelease, like a backport, belongs on a non-latest dist-tag through a separate path that is not built. CONFIRMED by opum-agent 2026-09-28; ADR amendment in opum-doc refuse-a-lore-quest-promotion-that-would-move-npm-latest-backwards.md (cite by ref once landed).

implementationNotes: SECOND ROUTE, from the LCLI-617 reviewer at #354 head dc7dbc40, measured there. A PRERELEASE --version, e.g. 1.0.0-beta.1, is accepted by SEMVER at promote-latest.mjs:1141 and :1178. Nothing in main() refuses it before the record is written, and at head the record is then refused by R1 on both resume and --rollback. So it strands a partial promotion exactly like the older-version case. Base 84f60e84 accepted it. The reviewer's suggested fix covers both routes: on a fresh run, validate plan.record with {version} BEFORE the first registry write. Scope this task to refuse, before any write, both a --version older than the current latest AND a --version that is not plain X.Y.Z (latest only ever takes a release). Pair the second clause with quest-cli too.

WHERE THE ADR (blob 2ca40316) AND THE TASK TEXT DIFFER, ADR wins: (1) the ADR's Status and Consequences attribute the plan-time refusal of an older --version to LCLI-617/#354, but at d1a0e320 LCLI-617 shipped only the resume/rollback half (validateRecord's newer-prior rule); its own comment says 'planPromotion does NOT itself refuse an older --version'. The plan-time gate lands here. (2) Amendment 1 fixes the mechanism as ONE gate (validateRecord on plan.record) 'rather than a second, parallel check'; the brief asked whether an earlier argv-time refusal is better, and the ADR's choice governs, so none is added. (3) A consequence neither text names: because the verdict is validateRecord's, a fresh run also refuses when a package's CURRENT latest is not a plain X.Y.Z (it would write a record resume and rollback refuse). quest-cli #369 has the same consequence by construction. (4) No conflict on equal-to-latest: ADR leaves it to existing semantics; task AC2 says keep them.

AC5 PREMISE FALSIFIED, measured through main() with an in-memory world: a prerelease --version (1.0.0-beta.1, 0.12.0-rc.1, 0.12.0+build.7) NEVER reaches planPromotion. Step 2's readArtifact runs compareLauncherTarballs, whose versionPairProblem (scripts/launcher-equivalence.mjs:61, landed by LCLI-621 bb8b2662, an ancestor of #354's base 84f60e84) refuses any X that is not a final MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, exit 1, zero registry writes, no record, and before any npm dist-tag read. So the reviewer's 'nothing in main() refuses it before the record is written' (and ADR Amendment 1's premise that it 'gets written into the promotion record') measured the SEMVER lines at :1141/:1178, not the path. The refusal message there is 'launcher equivalence (artifact) could not be measured: version "X" is not a final MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version' -- it does NOT say a prerelease belongs on a non-latest dist-tag, so AC5's message clause is unmet through main() and the new gate's prerelease clause is reachable only by calling planPromotion directly. Implemented per the ADR anyway (one gate, no second argv-time check, ADR wins); tests pin the artifact-gate refusal through main() and the gate's prerelease clause on planPromotion directly. DESIGN QUESTION for the orchestrator: add an argv-time RELEASE_VERSION refusal carrying the prerelease wording (verdict-neutral, message-only), or amend AC5/the ADR to record that the artifact gate already covers it. quest-cli's main() also qualifies the bundle before planPromotion, so the same may hold there -- not measured here.
